title: BCCWJ-MEG
description: This dataset comprises MEG recordings from 35 Japanese native speakers who read Japanese newspaper articles word by word, as part of the BCCWJ-Brain collection. Alongside fMRI and EEG datasets acquired from separate groups using the same stimuli, this MEG dataset enables cross-modality comparisons of language processing with high temporal resolution. Structural T1-weighted MRI images were also collected for source localization purposes.
methods_description: Continuous MEG was recorded with a 200-channel whole-head MEG system with axial gradiometers (RIOCH Ltd., Tokyo, Japan) in a shielded room at a sampling rate of 1,000 Hz with an online low-pass filter of 200 Hz. T1-weighted images were collected with slice thickness of 1 mm, field of view of 256 × 256 mm, matrix size of 368 × 368, TR of 1,100 ms, and TE of 5.1 ms; facial structures were removed using PyDeface. Stimuli (20 Japanese newspaper articles) were presented word by word via RSVP in PsychoPy, each for 500 ms followed by a 500 ms blank screen, in randomized article order. Preprocessing used MNE-Python and Eelbrain: a CALM filter was applied, data were combined with digitized files and converted to raw.fif, ICA was applied to remove ocular artifacts on 0.1–40 Hz bandpass filtered data, epochs were extracted from -100 to 1000 ms relative to word onset, downsampled to 200 Hz, and baseline-corrected using the -100 to 0 ms interval.
